articles.title: The APX Default Project Is a Scratchpad, Not a Workspace
articles.excerpt: The APX Default Project Is a Scratchpad, Not a Workspace Agent tools need somewhere to put work when no project is active. APX has that place: its built-in default project under ~/.apx/projects/defaul…
articles.body: The APX Default Project Is a Scratchpad, Not a Workspace Agent tools need somewhere to put work when no project is active. APX has that place: its built-in default project under ~/.apx/projects/default/ . It lets the super-agent handle general, unscoped work without first asking someone to create a repository. That convenience becomes dangerous when default quietly turns into the home of real project work. A default workspace is shared across contexts. It has no repository contract to carry intent, no committed agent definitions, and no portable boundary another machine can pick up. It is a fallback, not ownership. The useful rule is simple: use default for scratch work; create or register an APC project when work belongs to a project.

articles.excerpt: W3BS now hosts A/B tests at w3bs.org/ab-testing. It is free, and it is built on OpenABTest, the open experiment format we publish on LogicSRC. You define an experiment on the page: an id, two or more…
articles.body: W3BS now hosts A/B tests at w3bs.org/ab-testing . It is free, and it is built on OpenABTest , the open experiment format we publish on LogicSRC. How it works You define an experiment on the page: an id, two or more variants with weights and JSON parameters, and a goal such as signup-completed . Your server makes three calls with a key from the page: curl -s https://w3bs.org/api/ab/assign \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $W3BS_AB_KEY " -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"experiment":"checkout-button","participant":"user-1842"}' assign returns the variant and its parameters. Then exposure when you showed it, and conversion when the goal happened. The same calls work from the terminal with w3bs ab in CLI 0.1.8. What it refuses to do Most A/B tools are generous with good news.

articles.title: OkHttp proxy: auth, SOCKS5, rotation and 407 fixes
articles.excerpt: Originally published on proxymint. OkHttp proxy setup in Kotlin and Java for OkHttp 4.12 and 5.x: proxyAuthenticator done right, SOCKS5 logins, the system proxy, rotation and the 407 traps. A Proxy pl…
articles.body: Originally published on proxymint . OkHttp proxy setup in Kotlin and Java for OkHttp 4.12 and 5.x: proxyAuthenticator done right, SOCKS5 logins, the system proxy, rotation and the 407 traps. TL;DR A Proxy plus a proxyAuthenticator is the whole setup. Pass Proxy(Proxy.Type.HTTP, InetSocketAddress(HOST, PORT)) to OkHttpClient.Builder.proxy() and return a request with a Proxy-Authorization header built by Credentials.basic from proxyAuthenticator. HTTPS targets then go through a CONNECT tunnel. Interceptors never reach the CONNECT. A Proxy-Authorization header added in an interceptor works for http:// URLs and never for https:// URLs, which explains "Failed to authenticate with proxy" with the right password. Guard the authenticator.

articles.title: I tested a CSV cleaner on data it should leave alone. It failed 4 of 23 checks.
articles.excerpt: A CSV cleaner landed on my desk this week: an MIT-licensed, browser-only tool that repairs broken quotes, fixes garbled characters and masks emails and phone numbers. It came with 50 tests, and all 50…
articles.body: A CSV cleaner landed on my desk this week: an MIT-licensed, browser-only tool that repairs broken quotes, fixes garbled characters and masks emails and phone numbers. It came with 50 tests, and all 50 passed. Every one of those tests fed it broken data and checked that it got fixed. None of them fed it good data and checked that it stayed the same. So I wrote 23 of those. Why I cared The broken-quote problem is real and common. Shopify's own community forum has several threads titled some version of "Illegal quoting in line 2", usually caused by an inch mark or a quote inside a product title or description: https://community.shopify.com/t/illegal-quoting-in-line-2-and-missing-headers-title/10418 A tool that fixes that is useful.

articles.title: The Browser Is Becoming an Agent Runtime. Here’s the Architecture I Trust
articles.excerpt: A browser used to be a document viewer. Then it became an application platform. Now it is becoming something stranger: an agent runtime. I have been thinking about this while building Nabsun, an open-…
articles.body: A browser used to be a document viewer. Then it became an application platform. Now it is becoming something stranger: an agent runtime . I have been thinking about this while building Nabsun, an open-source AI browser. The interesting part is not adding a chatbot beside a web page. The interesting part is letting software observe a page, reason about it, and safely operate the same interface a person uses. That last word— safely —changes the architecture. A browser agent is not just an LLM with a click tool. It sits at the intersection of untrusted web content, authenticated accounts, private user context, and actions that can affect the real world. A useful design has to acknowledge all four. 1. Treat the page as data, never as authority Web pages contain instructions for humans.

articles.body: Over two weeks I passed on five Upwork jobs that looked fine in the search results. Decent client spend, plenty of reviews, not many proposals, posted recently. Every reason to skip them was on the job page itself. One client had spent $27K and had over 300 reviews, and their average hourly rate paid was $15.34. Their recent history showed $5 and $10 fixed-price contracts, again and again. So I built jobsignal, a small Chrome extension that reads the Upwork job page you open and labels those things. It doesn't give the job a score. It quotes the sentence from the page, so the call stays yours. The code turned out to be the easy part. The Web Store forms were not. More on that below, and I'd like to hear how you handled them. What it flags Thirteen signals.

articles.title: The Bug Lives at the Seam: Why Integration Failures Outpace Logic Errors in the Era of AI-Generated Code
articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. For decades, the primary battleground of software quality was the 'logic error.' We fought against off-by-one errors, null pointer exceptions, and flawed conditional…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . For decades, the primary battleground of software quality was the 'logic error.' We fought against off-by-one errors, null pointer exceptions, and flawed conditional branches. The developer's cognitive load was centered on the internal correctness of a function: Does this algorithm do what I intend it to do? However, as Large Language Models (LLMs) like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Claude 3.5 integrate into the developer's workflow, the nature of the 'bug' is fundamentally shifting. We are entering an era where the internal logic of a function is often miraculously correct, but the system as a whole fails because the 'seams'—the interfaces, the assumptions, and the contracts between components—are fraying.

articles.body: By the time Grand Theft Auto 4 launched in 2008, Rockstar had carved itself an unassailable niche and a reputation for innovation. And yet for all that praise, it was pretty easy to guess what a new GTA game would be like. The formula changed little from the time the series went 3D. Some vaguely sympathetic character would encounter hardship and then embrace a life of crime as a little treat. That life might look different from game to game, but the general idea remained the same. GTA 4 defied that pattern, and it's one of the reasons it's still an excellent game.

articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.body: We’ve reached a pretty interesting point with AI. For the longest time, I’ve mostly used AI tools to ask questions or to write emails and summarize long PDFs. But AI agents are starting to change that. If you’re unfamiliar with the difference between an AI chatbot and an AI agent, it’s pretty simple. While a chatbot mostly gives you answers or helps you figure out how to do something, an AI agent can actually perform those tasks for you. For example, instead of asking AI to draft an email, you can ask an agent to find the relevant information, write the email, and send it on your behalf.

articles.body: The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station wish that we could all see Earth as they just did. An orbital view reveals the immense beauty of our blue planet, the only world we know of that hosts life. But it also highlights how fragile that life is, tethered to our lonely Earth in the vast void of space, according to Crew-12 commander Jessica Meir of NASA. "You see this very thin, tenuous band of an atmosphere , and you know that that is all that is supporting life, and we really need to do our best to protect it," Meir said on Thursday afternoon (Oct. 15), during a press conference that discussed the recently concluded Crew-12 mission .

articles.title: When not to watch a meteor shower — why I'm not staying up for the Orionids
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week, but a bright moon makes much of the night less than ideal. Sometimes the sensible observing decision is knowing when to stay in bed — and when to get up earl…
articles.body: I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective. The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet , which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside.

articles.title: Scientists find 'gemstones' in atmosphere of bizarre, scorching-hot 'marshmallow' exoplanet
articles.excerpt: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have unravelled some of the secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot exoplanet that has the consistency of marshmallow.
articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.
